attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post, endorsed.

semantics.note: Keeps every clause, the word 'fully', and the hedge 'effectively nobody else'. It is a present-tense description of both labs.

contract.note: Leaving hyperscalers out of 'nobody else' and reading 'fully' literally both follow his own wording. A two-year period drawn from his context is reasonable. Not scoring the characterizations is fair.

evidence.note: Reputable report of OpenAI's $6.4B all-equity io deal. It directly supports the stock-acquisition clause.

Company disclosure dated before the post: Anthropic announces its own $50B data-center investment. Under the contract this contradicts 'fully paid for by other companies'. Who actually finances it is not documented.
xAI's planned Colossus 2 scale. Partly planned and not compared with the labs, so it does not settle 'effectively nobody else'.

reviews.rationale: The stock-acquisition part holds: OpenAI did a $6.4B all-equity deal. 'Infrastructure fully paid for by other companies' is contradicted by Anthropic's announced $50B investment in its own data centers. The scale part ('effectively nobody else') is unresolved because there is no capacity comparison. The characterizations are not scored.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his post.

semantics.note: The surrounding text identifies the 'guy' as Cherny. The figure 'upwards of $130,000 a month' is kept.

contract.note: He named no pricing basis. Valuing internal use at list price, and reading 'allowed' as actual use that went unstopped, is the ordinary reading. The period comes from the talk he cites.

evidence.note: Transcript of the cited talk: Cherny says he used about 8B tokens since March. With no split by token type or model, it cannot be priced.
Unsourced personal-blog estimate of about $75k a month. It gives no pricing basis, so it cannot settle the claim.

reviews.rationale: Cherny's own count is about 8B tokens since March. Without the split into input, output and cache tokens, or the model and tier, that cannot be turned into a list-price dollar figure. The only dollar estimate is an unsourced blog. Nothing in the packet confirms or rules out $130k a month.

semantics.note: The faithful version, without the added 'with AI' or 'despite being false'. The main thrust is causal market psychology. 'Nobody' is hyperbole.

contract.note: Treating 'nobody' as hyperbole and the mechanism as unobservable is fair. The stock-movement clause is trivially true. The speaker gives no measure.

evidence.note: Shows SaaS stocks fell on the AI-replaces-software story. It does not test why the story took hold.
Cursor replaced a small CMS, not SAP, Salesforce or Office 365. Consistent with his point, but not a test of it.
Klarna's partial in-house build, and its CEO's clarification. One partial case cannot test a hyperbolic 'nobody'.

reviews.rationale: This is a rhetorical, causal claim about why a market story caught on. 'Nobody' has no threshold, and the bias mechanism cannot be observed. The stock-movement clause is trivially true. The evidence shows stocks moved and only isolated partial in-house builds, which does not allow fair scoring.

semantics.note: Keeps the firm 'very clear' allegation and the hedged 'I believe' guess about S&M. Only the firm part is scorable.

contract.note: Counting any flattering classification as 'moved around numbers' leans slightly toward the speaker. The packet does not settle the claim under either reading.

evidence.note: Confirms the 2025 cost of revenue and S&M figures. It says nothing on how costs were classified or whether anything was shifted.
Analyst inference that free-user inference sits in S&M. It is not a disclosure, and it does not show numbers were moved to flatter results.

reviews.rationale: There is no public filing, notes, restatement, or reputable report documenting how OpenAI classified inference compute, or any reclassification. The line items are confirmed, and one analyst guesses free-user inference is in S&M. Nothing settles whether numbers were moved to look better. The 'I believe' part is hedged and not scored.
